newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea Telecom listing slated for first half 1997.
newsitem.headline: Korea Telecom listing slated for first half 1997.

text.p: South Korea on Thursday set a time frame for listing Korea Telecom in a move analysts said appeared aimed at luring more investors to the state-run firm after two previous lacklustre subscriptions.
They said the plan may work but warned that the new share supply could add pressure to the already bearish stock market.

The Ministry of Finance and Economy, unveiling a plan to sell 9.65 million Korea Telecom shares this month, said the firm would be listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in the first half of 1997. The shares, valued at about 360 billion won ($434 million), will be sold in an auction on November 28 and 29.
"The government has to sell the shares to raise revenue," said Bahn Young-one, telecommunications analyst at Ssangyong Investment Securities.

The government has repeatedly postponed listing the telephone service provider since 1995, citing weak market conditions. The market has declined nearly 25 percent since its year high in May. The stock index closed almost flat at 744.91 on Thursday.
"The government can't delay it anymore," Bahn said. "No one is willing to lock up cash in shares uncertain of listing."

The ministry said the auction represents 3.35 percent of the telephone service provider's outstanding shares. The government now owns around 79 percent of Korea Telecom, which has a monopoly on South Korea's local telephone service, and holds the lion's share of the long distance and data communications markets.
The government has been selling Korea Telecom shares since 1993 in a move to privatise state-run companies.
Two previous Korea Telecom share auctions in October and earlier this month were limited to institutional investors and corporations. They were undersubscribed due to the dull stock market.
Uncertainty over when Korea Telecom would be listed also damaged the stock's popularity, analysts said.
Individual investors will be eligible to participate in the auction this time.

"News that the stock will be listed in the first half will attract individual buyers to the auction next week," said Bahn of Ssangyong. "We'll see a better response this time than the last two subscriptions."
The finance ministry is also betting it will be able to attract more buyers this time.
"We have opened the doors for individuals this time, and they may want to invest in a company with high profitability," said a ministry official.
Korea Telecom, which has a paid-in capital of 1.44 trillion won, or 288 billion shares, posted a net profit of 419 billion won on a turnover of 6.36 trillion last year.

Bill Hunsaker of ING-Barings Securities criticised the government's move, saying telecom companies were likely to face slower growth in the future due to tougher competition and reduced long distance call rates.
Though analysts and brokers were concerned that the fragile market environment would be hurt by a deluge of new supply, they added that few expect the listing to go ahead as scheduled.
"The market is so bearish that investors expect the government to push off the listing again," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities.
